title: Footer span inherits accent color from theme, invisible on dark footer

patterns: accent-colored text on dark footer background
theme switch makes footer span invisible

rule.summary: When a footer has a dark background, any `<span>` inside it must NOT rely on the theme's `--clr-accent` color — accent is often bright over dark and produces < 3:1 contrast.
rule.details: In the base CSS, `.footer span` uses `color: var(--clr-accent)`. On a `background: var(--clr-primary-dark)` footer, the accent color (#3182ce, #38bdf8, #52b788, etc.) can drop below 3:1 contrast. Each theme MUST override `.footer span { color: var(--clr-white) }` or another high-contrast value.
rule.check: `window.getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.footer span')).color` contrast against `.footer` background color — must be >= 4.5:1 for normal text.
rule.fix: Add `.footer span { color: var(--clr-white); }` to each theme CSS.

evidence.description: Azul theme: added `.footer span { color: var(--clr-white) }` and verified 44/44
